input.title: The commitment picker can silently jump to the current hour when the panel opens
input.body:
Found while investigating the `ui-requirements` flake on `main` (run [31506304596](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/31506304596) attempt 1, which reported `# pass 95 / # fail 2`).

## The bug

`openPanel` positions the constraint panel's time wheels one `requestAnimationFrame` after the panel is un-hidden. When that frame finds no scrollable layout yet, `scrollTo` is a no-op and `scrollTop` stays `0`. The settle handler in `buildConstraintPanel` then reads `0` back as the user picking `hours[0]` and calls `setConstraintTime` — moving the commitment to the **current hour**, where usually nothing starts.

The picker then renders `"No shows start exactly then. Nearest:"`, and **nothing ever re-renders the list**, so the wrong state is sticky for the rest of the session until the user scrolls a wheel themselves.

Confirmed directly against the running page: with the hour wheel clamped to `0` and one scroll event dispatched, the picker goes from

- `shows start at 21:30`, 2 picks, Masala present → `shows start at 19:30`, 0 picks, `.picklist-empty`, Masala gone

and is still in that state 3 s later.

## Why it matters beyond CI

This is user-visible, not just a test artifact: on a slow device or a busy frame, opening "change your next commitment" lands on the current hour and claims nothing starts then. The user's actual default (now + 2 h) is silently discarded.

## How it surfaced

Screen case `now-list.6.8` drives this panel and clicks `.show-pick:has-text("Masala")`. When the jump happens the pick never exists, so the click burns its full 30 s and fails as a `TimeoutError` — not a golden mismatch. It passed on re-run and passes locally, which is what made it look like a golden flake.

## Note on the existing guard

The close path already guards the same clamp-to-0 artifact:

```js
// Closing the panel display:nones the wheels, which clamps their
// scrollTop to 0 and fires one last scroll event — a layout artifact,
// not the user picking hours[0].
if (el.offsetParent === null) return;
```

The opening direction has the same hazard, with only a bare rAF between un-hiding and scrolling.

## Also seen in that run, not covered here

`now-filters.5.3` failed in the same run with a genuine pixel diff (`312 of 50853 pixels differ (0.61%)`). That is a separate, still-undiagnosed defect — not reproduced locally in 25 renders under 6× CPU load, and its diff artifact was unreachable from the agent sandbox (the egress proxy denies `productionresultssa3.blob.core.windows.net`). Filed here only so it isn't lost; it needs the diff artifact or a reproducing run before anyone changes code for it.

input.body:
Closes #335.

Investigating the `ui-requirements` flake on `main`. **It is not a golden-tolerance problem**, and it was not one failure — see "Premises that turned out wrong" below.

## What actually failed

Run [31506304596](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/31506304596) attempt 1 on `main` (`4ecd992`) reported `# pass 95 / # fail 2`:

| # | case | failure |
|---|---|---|
| 51 | `now-list.6.8` | `page.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` waiting for `.show-pick:has-text("Masala")` |
| 36 | `now-filters.5.3` | `312 of 50853 pixels differ (0.61%)` |

Only 5.3 is a pixel diff. 6.8 is a `TimeoutError` — the element never appears, so no comparator threshold could ever have affected it.

## Root cause of `now-list.6.8`

`openPanel` positions the time wheels one `requestAnimationFrame` after the panel is un-hidden. When that frame finds no scrollable layout yet, `scrollTo` is a no-op and `scrollTop` stays `0`. The settle handler then reads `0` back as the user picking `hours[0]`, and `setConstraintTime` moves the commitment to the current hour — where usually nothing starts. The picker renders `"No shows start exactly then"`, and **nothing ever re-renders the list**, so the state is sticky and the subsequent click burns the full 30 s.

Confirmed directly against the running page: with the hour wheel clamped to `0` and one scroll event dispatched, the picker goes from

- `shows start at 21:30`, 2 picks, Masala present → `shows start at 19:30`, 0 picks, `.picklist-empty`, Masala gone

and is still in that state 3 s later.

The close path already guards this exact clamp-to-0 artifact (`if (el.offsetParent === null) return;` — "a layout artifact, not the user picking hours[0]"). The opening direction had the same hazard with only a bare rAF between un-hiding and scrolling.

This is user-visible, not just a test artifact — see #335.

## The fix

Generalise the guard the close path already carries. Every programmatic position matches `state.selectedTime` by construction, so reading one back can only repeat it or corrupt it — **only a wheel the user has actually touched since it was last positioned is read**. `scrollWheelTo` clears the flag; drags, wheel/trackpad turns, touches and the arrow keys set it. `scrollWheelTo` also re-applies its target on the next frame when layout blocked the first attempt, so the wheel never sits displaying an hour the state disagrees with.

The case's `waitForTimeout(400)` is replaced with a wait on the picker actually resting at 21:30. A fixed sleep cannot tell "settled" from "settled on the wrong hour" — which is why this surfaced 30 s later as a selector timeout instead of where it happened.

**No golden is changed.** The fix makes the behaviour the goldens already encode deterministic, which is what this repo's rule asks for (see below).

## Verification

- Real interaction still drives the picker: a wheel turn moves `21:30 → 22:30`, `ArrowDown` on minutes → `22:35`.
- The layout-artifact scroll is now ignored: picker holds `21:30` / 2 picks / Masala.
- `npm run test:ui` — **97/97**. `npm test` — **274/274**. `scripts/verify.sh` — clean.

## Premises that turned out wrong

Flagging these because they shaped the original brief:

1. **`main` is not red.** Run `31506304596` is on attempt 2, which passed; the list API reports only the latest attempt, so `main`'s check is green. The red was attempt 1. The run before it (`628cbc8`) was *cancelled* by the `cancel-in-progress` concurrency group, not failed — so "green at 05:05 then failed on the next two runs" is really "green, cancelled, red-then-green-on-re-run".
2. **It was 2 failures, not 1**, and of two different kinds.
3. **The repo does not want a tolerance.** `shared/compare.js` is zero-tolerance by design, and `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-requirements/RULES.md` says explicitly: *"When the comparison ever flaps, the fix is more determinism, not a tolerance: the comparator stays at zero diff."* The canon `writing-tests` skill's "allow a small diff tolerance" line is about browser goldens in general; this repo has deliberately overridden it by pinning Chromium, fonts, clock, geolocation and randomness. So loosening the comparator would have contradicted a standing decision — and would not have touched 6.8 anyway.

## Not fixed here: `now-filters.5.3`

I have **not** diagnosed the 312-pixel diff, and I have not guessed at a fix for it.

- Not reproduced locally: 25 consecutive renders under 6× CPU load on a 4-core box, all pixel-identical to the golden.
- The `requirements-failure-artifacts` diff image is unreachable from this environment — the agent proxy denies `productionresultssa3.blob.core.windows.net` (`403` to `CONNECT`), so I could not see which pixels moved.
- Ruled out: the panel's `.seg-count` values are a stable `0/0/0/0/0/0` at capture time, and `tweenCount` (the one animated counter) is not used by the price panel.

It is a separate defect from 6.8 and wants the diff artifact — or a run that reproduces it — before anyone changes code for it. Re-baselining it would be an unreviewed behaviour change, so I left it alone. Recorded in #335 so it isn't lost.

## Complete

**PR #325** — merged (squash, `5601a86`). Verified first that all three files sit under `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/` and genuinely cannot reach a UI golden, and that the 2026-08-11 re-run was green.

**The flake** — investigated and fixed, but it wasn't the problem described:

- **`main` was not red.** The run is on attempt 2, which passed; the API reports only the latest attempt. The run before it was *cancelled* by the `cancel-in-progress` concurrency group, not failed.
- **Two failures, not one**, of different kinds.
- **The repo forbids a tolerance.** `compare.js` is zero-tolerance by design, and `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-requirements/RULES.md` states: *"When the comparison ever flaps, the fix is more determinism, not a tolerance."* The canon `writing-tests` guidance is real but this repo deliberately overrode it by pinning Chromium, fonts, clock, geolocation and randomness.

**Root cause of `now-list.6.8`** — not a pixel diff at all but a 30 s `TimeoutError`. The wheels are positioned one rAF after the panel is un-hidden; when that frame finds no scrollable layout, `scrollTo` no-ops, `scrollTop` stays 0, and the settle handler reads 0 back as the user picking `hours[0]`. The commitment jumps to the current hour, the picker says "No shows start exactly then", and nothing re-renders the list — so it's sticky. Confirmed against the live page: clamp the hour wheel, fire one scroll, and it goes from `21:30`/2 picks/Masala to `19:30`/0 picks and stays there. This is user-visible on any slow frame, not just in CI.

The fix generalises the guard the close path already carries — only a wheel the user actually touched is read back. Real interaction still works (`21:30 → 22:30 → 22:35`). No golden changed. 97/97 UI, 274/274 unit, `verify.sh` clean, and both PR checks green.

**Artifacts:** issue **#335** (the product bug), PR **#333** (the fix) — left open for your review, since unlike #325 it changes product behaviour.

**Not fixed:** `now-filters.5.3`'s 312-pixel diff. I couldn't reproduce it in 25 renders under 6× CPU load, and the diff artifact is unreachable — the egress proxy returns 403 for `productionresultssa3.blob.core.windows.net`. I ruled out the obvious candidates but won't guess, and re-baselining it would be exactly the unreviewed behaviour change you warned against. It's recorded in #335 so it isn't lost; it needs the artifact or a reproducing run.

Earlier I offered to watch #333 for CI and review comments — that offer stands if you want it, but I haven't subscribed without your say-so.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
